shape: This session, closing a small self-diagnostic item (AUT-PD-056) that turned out to expose a real defect in this same session's own receipt-writing practice.
took: AUT-PD-056 — verify CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is set inside a scheduled-routine session (RT-AUTONOMY, free, $0, closing).
took_what: Checked `env | grep CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `session_cap.session_id_read()` directly from inside this genuine scheduled-Routine session: CONFIRMED SET, real value `1ef8c95a-24d8-5fea-a441-6295a15751f9`. Then ran `python3 research/autonomy/session_cap.py --check` and got 'this session has written 0 receipt(s) against a cap of 2' -- despite this session having already written 8 real receipts earlier this cycle-cluster. Root cause: every prior receipt this session wrote (CYC-0033-schedule through CYC-0056-schedule) used the literal placeholder string 'scheduled-routine-session' as `session_id`, which is exactly what `session_cap.PLACEHOLDER_IDS` exists to reject, instead of the real env var. The research-loop skill was already updated today (by a concurrent session) to instruct the correct practice; this session had not caught up to it. Fixed going forward: this receipt (and its own id, computed via `ids.next_receipt('research/autonomy/receipts', session_cap.session_id() or '')` as the skill now instructs) uses the real session id in both the filename and the session_id field.
changed: research/autonomy/research-ledger.json: closed AUT-PD-056 (done), with the concrete evidence and the practice-gap finding recorded.
This session's own future receipts: now use the real CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID for both the receipt id discriminator and the session_id field, per the research-loop skill's already-updated instruction.
what_i_got_wrong: This session wrote 'scheduled-routine-session' as a literal placeholder into every receipt's session_id field for its entire duration, despite the real env var being available the whole time -- inherited from an earlier convention without re-checking whether a better mechanism existed. AUT-PD-056's own investigation is what caught it, by the accident of the ledger item itself asking exactly the question this session's practice had gotten wrong. Lesson: when a skill file is noted as having been updated by a concurrent session mid-cycle-cluster, re-read the specific section rather than continuing on the version read at session start.
